title: Contextual ephemeral runbook tuner and probe prioritizer
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds an opt-in ephemeral runbook tuner which suggests compact runbook step orders and probe priorities based on recent telemetry; includes a sandboxed replay harness for validating suggestions before rollout. Feature is off by default and gated behind incident-bot.feature.ephemeral_tuner=true.
description:
Context and motivation: On many post-incident reviews we see runbooks that are either stale (steps in wrong order), over-verbose (too many low-value probes), or brittle (expensive probes executed too early). This PR adds a small, production-safe system that proposes ephemeral runbook reorderings and probe prioritization using only short-lived telemetry windows. The goal is not to auto-modify canonical runbooks, but to produce actionable, human-reviewable suggestions and to let responders rehearse suggested flows in a sandbox before applying changes.

What this PR does (single-string description): - Adds a lightweight runbook tuner that ingests the last 30 minutes of relevant telemetry (traces, p95 latencies, error spikes, alerts) and scores each runbook step for: expected time-to-signal, evidence-value (how often the probe returns a decisive signal), and cost (estimated resource impact). - Produces a ranked suggestion list and a compact alternative runbook (ephemeral) that reorders high-value quick probes first, defers noisy/expensive probes to later, and inserts safety-checks for destructive remediations. - Exposes a /v1/sandbox/replay endpoint and a local replay harness (incident-bot/sandbox/replay_harness.py) so on-call can execute the suggested sequence against a mocked telemetry replay (no write effects) and see a summarized delta vs the canonical runbook. - Adds conservative safety gates: suggestions are only generated for runbooks with >= 5 historical incidents and only when telemetry window passes a stability check (no active high-velocity noise). Feature toggles live under incident-bot.feature.ephemeral_tuner and incident-bot.sandbox.enabled.

Checklist (what's in this PR): - [x] core tuner algorithm and scoring (incident-bot/runbook/tuner.py) - [x] sandboxed replay harness and HTTP endpoint (incident-bot/sandbox/replay_harness.py, incident-bot/api/sandbox_handler.py) - [x] UI signals (compact suggestion payload only; UI-side will be in a follow-up PR) - [x] unit + integration tests for scoring and replay simulator - [x] e2e rehearsal test that runs a real incident trace through sandbox (CI flakiness noted, retried once) - [x] config flags and docs (docs/runbook-tuner.md)

Summary of commits: - 8c4a5b2: initial tuner scaffolding and schema - 2f9b12d: implement scoring heuristics and cost model - c3d7f44: sandbox replay harness + deterministic mock telemetry - 7eaf811: add safety-gates and feature flag hooks - 9b0d22e: tests and CI flakiness mitigation - b10a6cc: docs and release notes

Files changed (high level): - incident-bot/runbook/tuner.py (new) - incident-bot/runbook/score_model.py (new) - incident-bot/sandbox/replay_harness.py (new) - incident-bot/api/sandbox_handler.py (new) - incident-bot/config/feature_flags.yaml (updated) - docs/runbook-tuner.md (new) - tests/runbook/test_tuner_scoring.py (new) - tests/sandbox/test_replay_harness.py (new) - examples/sandbox/example_replay_payloads.json (new) - incident-bot/metrics/metrics_registry.py (updated) - incident-bot/ci/rehearsal_e2e.yml (updated) - incident-bot/README.md (update: quickstart for sandbox)

Design notes and safe-guards (important): - Non-destructive: ephemeral suggestions are stored only in-memory and expire after 24 hours; they never auto-apply to canonical runbooks. - Low blast radius: tuning only runs if the number of matching historical incidents >= 5 and the telemetry sample passes a simple signal/noise ratio test (implemented in tuner.is_stable_window). - Explainability: each suggestion item includes attributes {reason, evidence_count, estimated_time_saved_ms, estimated_cost_delta} so responders can quickly decide. - Human-in-the-loop: UI will show a "Run in sandbox" button; the replay harness returns a deterministic summary and an optional timeline to assist live rehearsals. - Auditable: suggestion generation events are logged to the incident-bot audit log with non-sensitive fingerprints for later review.

Testing and CI: Unit and integration tests added. One CI run initially showed a flaky e2e rehearsal test (timing-dependent); we pinned the mock time source and retried. CI: passing (build, lint, unit, integration, rehearsal-e2e). See CI notes below for the transient failure and resolution.

Review conversation (condensed single-string): - Marcus Lee (reviewer): "Nice work — can we make the stability check stricter? I've seen windows that look stable but are actually churned by infra restarts." Aisha: "Agree, bumped the default threshold and exposed it as incident-bot.tuner.stability_threshold (0.7 -> 0.85) and added an integration test that simulates infra restarts." - Evelyn Chen: "How do we prevent suggestions from being noisy for small teams?" Aisha: "Added a min-historical-incidents config (default 5) and a rate limiter (max 1 suggestion per runbook per 24h)." - Rohit Singh: "Make sure audit logs don't contain PII." Aisha: "Logs only include hashed fingerprints and non-identifying counters; added a test to validate no raw identifiers are written." - Marcus Lee (final): "LGTM after the stability threshold change and docs update" (approved).

CI status and notes: - Initial CI: one failing e2e (tests/sandbox/test_replay_harness.py) due to non-deterministic mock clock. - Fix: replace time.time() usage with injected monotonic clock in the harness and add a deterministic mock in tests. - Final CI: all checks passing (build: pass, unit: pass, integration: pass, rehearsal-e2e: pass).

Rollout plan: - Feature is behind two flags; start internal alpha (on-call team) for 2 weeks, gather feedback and adjust scoring weights. - After alpha, enable opt-in for a small set of customers in dedicated deployment via infra toggle. - Full public rollout only after UX follow-up PR (UI for reviewing suggestions) and an additional 2-week soak.

Operational metrics to watch after rollout: - suggestion_accept_rate (how often suggested order was adopted by humans) - average_time_saved_ms (estimate from tuner) - suggestion_false_positive_rate (manual rejects / suggestions) - replay_success_rate (sandbox runs that complete without errors) - incident_response_latency_90 (primary SLO to verify no regression)

Backward compatibility and config: - Defaults preserve current behavior: feature flags off, no change to canonical runbooks or existing endpoints. - All new endpoints are namespaced under /v1/sandbox and require incident-bot.sandbox.enabled=true.

Follow-ups (tracked in Linear): - ENG-2049: UI for viewing & approving suggestions - ENG-2050: Auto-snapshot suggested runbook metadata to incident timeline (opt-in) - ENG-2077: Expand evidence extractors to include logs and runbook outcome classification

Why this is different from previous work: Rather than trying to auto-edit canonical runbooks, this PR focuses on a safe, ephemeral layer that helps responders rehearse and accept improvements with low friction. The replay harness gives a deterministic, no-op rehearsal path that hasn't been in the codebase before and reduces cognitive friction when trying suggestions.

Contact and owner: Aisha Patel (author) — tuned the scoring and drove the sandbox implementation.
